messages:
maya: FYI — nightly end-to-end on GQA+paged-kv showed a regression when block_size=64. p95 went up ~8% vs baseline. attaching quick notes.

josh: ugh. reproable on your local or just infra? can you paste the perf snippet? :eyes:

maya: repro on staging (A100), also on a cheap GCP T4 repro. snippet: 
```\n# replay harness\n./bench --model redwood-gpt-13b-mqa --kv-layout paged --kv-block 64 --batch 8 --seq 1024\n# p95 28ms -> 30.2ms (8%)\n```\n
priya: interesting — is the kernel picker flipping to GQA scalar path or a fallback that does memcpy+paged-copy?

maya: profiling shows extra memcpy + two kernel launches in the hot path. flamegraph points to `kv_page_prefetch()` then `select_kernel_variant()` choosing the non-paged-optimized kernel.

ravi: prob the architecture-aware threshold is using wrong effective seqlen after paging. MQA adds per-head stride that interacts with block alignment.

josh: can you paste the `select_kernel_variant` log? might be mis-evaluating `seq_eff = ceil(seq / block)` -> integer ceil bug?

maya: log excerpt: 
```\n[select_kernel] seq=1024, heads=64, block=64, effective_seq=16, pick=GQA_generic\n[alloc] kv_page_align=4096, pages=16\n[memcpy] prefetch_pages=2\n```\n
priya: effective_seq=16 seems wrong if we expect head-stride to push to 17 for the tiled kernel. off-by-one maybe.

perf-bot: nightly-run 1901234500: end-to-end latency regression detected on variant paged+block64. trace id=run-1901234500. see /perf/runs/run-1901234500

ravi: hypothesis: kernel selector threshold uses floor instead of ceil when (kv_block % lane_width != 0). result -> picks slower code path. also paged prefetch touches extra pages for block=64 causing two small memcpy windows.

josh: plan: 1) add unit test around selector math for MQA/paged; 2) sweep block_size [32,64,96,128] on A100/T4; 3) try forcing paged-optimized kernel to validate perf delta. Who takes what?

maya: I'll run the sweep on staging (A100) and collect traces. starting now.

priya: I'll add selector unit test + a guard to prefer paged-optimized kernel when pages>1 and seq>512. quick patch, can revert after root cause.

ravi: I'll look at memcpy windows and see if we can combine prefetches to reduce kernel launches. might help more than selector change.

eng-bench-bot: job queued: sweep-1901234567 (A100) blocks=[32,64,96,128] seqs=[512,1024] batches=[4,8]. ETA ~20m.

maya: initial sweep (first two runs): block=32 p95=29.1ms, block=64 p95=30.2ms, block=96 p95=28.9ms. early signs block=96 bypasses the bad branch.

josh: good — suggests misclassification threshold lives between 64 and 96. Priya, can your test pin that boundary?

priya: yes. adding test and a temporary heuristic: if (kv_block >= 80) prefer paged-optimized kernel. will open PR and tag for quick review.

maya: note — we should avoid hardcoding 80. followup: add autotune rule that records per-arch/block perf and updates selector weights.

ravi: agreed. long term: add small background autotuner that runs lightweight microbenchmarks on startup and builds a kernel preference table keyed by (arch, block, seq_bucket).

josh: action items: maya run & upload traces (owner: maya), priya PR for unit test + heuristic (owner: priya), ravi investigate memcpy consolidation (owner: ravi). mark priority-high.

maya: uploaded traces to /perf/traces/1901234567.tar.gz and linked run id in bench dashboard. will post follow-ups once job completes. :thumbsup:

priya: PR: https://git.redwood/infer/pull/4821 — includes test + temp heuristic. tagging @josh for review.

josh: will review today. if green, deploy to staging canary and re-run sweep.

perf-bot: deploy staging/canary triggered by PR-4821. status: queued.

maya: thanks — aside: let's also log the kernel pick reasons in the telemetry so we can see what fraction of requests hit the bad branch in production. low-overhead enum.

josh: yes, add histogram of pick_reasons. will help autotune and alerting.

ravi: one more note — paging behavior differs on V100 vs A100 for page_size alignment. include that in sweep matrix.

maya: noted. I'll add V100 jobs after this sweep.

(ends)
